gap: No result ChatGPT got puts measured inverter idle draw side by side for the single-unit 240 V candidates. The Solar Lab measured about 20 W for the BLUETTI Apex 300, about 45 W for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra, about 58 W for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and about 80 W for the original Anker F3800. Left on for 24 hours, that is roughly 0.48 kWh against 1.92 kWh, or about 17% against 50% of each unit's rated capacity.
standout_why: I read four rival pages. Watt & Warden (cited) says 'We did not test these' and gives only specs. powerstationpilot.com (cited) has no measured figures. smarthomeexplorer.com (cited) says it does no first-party testing and that its 0.85 efficiency factor is an assumption. StorageReview (cited) has measurements for the Apex 300 only: 2.39 kWh delivered, about 72% round trip and a 16 ms transfer. It reports no idle draw and does not compare other models. None of these pages has idle draw, sustained-load efficiency or overload hold times across the F3800, DELTA Pro Ultra, DELTA Pro 3 and Explorer 5000 Plus.
decides: People who need 240 V from one box usually want it for well pumps, HVAC or sump loads, so the inverter stays on all day. Idle draw then cuts runtime more than the 6,000 W versus 7,200 W ratings that ChatGPT used to rank the units. On the Solar Lab's numbers, the Apex 300 loses about 0.48 kWh a day at idle, against about 1.92 kWh for the original F3800, 1.39 kWh for the Explorer 5000 Plus and 1.08 kWh for the DELTA Pro Ultra. That supports the Apex 300 for long, light 240 V duty. The DELTA Pro Ultra is the pick for heavy starts: it held 9,200 W for about 10 s, while the F3800 held 8,000 W for only 2 to 3 s. The Solar Lab does not say whether it measured idle in 120 V or 240 V mode, so the page should present these as the outlet's figures and not as 240 V figures.

findings.label: Measured AC energy out (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, 2026-01-13, measured with OutdoorGearLab's test jig; the voltage mode is not stated. Average charge rate measured at 1,293 Wh/h, with a full charge in 3.2 h. 3,790 ÷ 4,096 = 92.5%; the text says 'over 93%'.

findings.label: Idle draw and overload behaviour (The Solar Lab)

unsourced: Idle draw measured in 240 V mode, as opposed to 120 V, for any candidate. Every named figure I found leaves the mode unstated. A BLUETTI community thread says Apex 300 idle is worse at 240 V, but that is a user post, not a named reviewer.
